paper: Davis & LeVeque 2020, ACM TOMS, DOI 10.1145/3392775 (adjoint-guided AMR for linear hyperbolic PDEs, Clawpack/AMRClaw)

open_questions.q: Does the adjoint-error flagging variant (paper §5, Fig. 12) yield a directly-proportional relationship between the flagging tolerance and the achievable relative error in the functional J, and does that proportionality hold across a 3+ decade tolerance sweep in both 1D and 2D?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md marks claim C5 ('tolerance in adjoint-error flagging directly controls achievable J-error') as only PARTIAL — the replication tested only the adjoint-magnitude variant. The paper's Fig. 11/12 shows adjoint-error is the strongest performer and the one whose tolerance most cleanly maps to J-error. Whether that proportionality is a genuine property of the estimator or an artifact of the specific tolerance range in the paper is not known from the current replication.
next_steps: In amrclaw/examples/acoustics_1d_adjoint/setrun.py, enable adjoint-error flagging (paper-specific code path in the adjoint_module; may require setting a distinct flag in the maintained Clawpack v5.9.2 source or backporting from v5.6.1).
Run a tolerance sweep spanning 10^-1 through 10^-6, computing J each time against a fixed Richardson tol=1e-6 reference.
Plot log(|J − J_ref| / J_ref) vs log(tol); slope ≈ 1 supports C5, slope ≠ 1 quantifies the deviation.
Repeat in 2D with a target-rectangle J on Example 3 geometry.

open_questions.q: How much of the observed 5.65× (total) / 7.82× (L3) 2D cost reduction persists across a full tolerance sweep, and does the crossover point between adjoint-magnitude and Richardson depend on the target-region size or geometry?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §4.2 reports C4 (the '2D advantage is dramatic') from a SINGLE tolerance pair (adjoint tol=0.04 vs Richardson tol=1e-3). The caveat list explicitly notes 'Only one 2D tolerance pair tested'. Without a sweep, the ratios could be peculiar to this pair, and the sensitivity of the advantage to target-region size (a point-spike vs a rectangle) is untested.
next_steps: In amrclaw/examples/acoustics_2d_adjoint/, run a 3×3 grid of (adjoint_tol, richardson_tol) pairings that produce matched final-time mass at 4 accuracy levels.
Report the (cells_richardson / cells_adjoint) ratio as a function of achieved accuracy — a monotone curve confirms the advantage is not a lucky pairing.
Vary the adjoint IC support: a δ-like point spike vs a Gaussian of width σ ∈ {0.1, 0.5, 1.0} vs a target rectangle. Report how the total-cell-count ratio scales with target-region area.

open_questions.q: Do the paper's exact Example 1 numbers (60 base cells, domain [-12,12], target x_p=7.5, t_f=34, Fig. 12 CPU curves) reproduce quantitatively when the domain and target are rebuilt to match, rather than using the smaller Clawpack-maintained didactic variant?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §4.1 caveat 3 explicitly notes the 1D replication used the maintained example (domain [-5,3], target x=1.5, t_f=15, 30 base cells), NOT paper Example 1's setup. The replication reproduces the DIRECTIONAL claim (adjoint < Richardson at matched J-error) but cannot compare absolute numbers to Fig. 12. It is genuinely open whether paper Example 1 as originally specified would give the same ordering (very likely) AND the same absolute CPU / cell-count magnitudes (unknown).
next_steps: Copy acoustics_1d_adjoint/ and modify setrun.py: domain [-12, 12], num_cells=60, t_final=34, adjoint IC Gaussian centered at 7.5.
Re-run the full tolerance sweep (adjoint-magnitude and Richardson).
Overlay the resulting error-vs-work curve on paper Fig. 12; report absolute-agreement fraction (log-scale offset) alongside directional agreement.

open_questions.q: Was the adjoint-flagging kernel (adjoint_module, flag2refine on the inner product q̂ᵀq, and the mapping from |q̂ᵀq| to the refinement decision) modified between Clawpack v5.6.1 (paper) and v5.9.2 (this replication) in ways that could shift the quantitative comparison of adjoint vs Richardson?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md caveat 1 flags the version drift (v5.6.1 → v5.9.2) but does not audit the adjoint-AMR source-code diff between those tags. If maintainers changed the inner-product weighting, the L3 threshold semantics, the stored-snapshot interpolation-in-time, or the flagging threshold arithmetic, this replication would be reproducing the MAINTAINED algorithm and not the paper's exact one.
next_steps: cd clawpack/amrclaw; git log --oneline v5.6.1..v5.9.2 -- src/2d/adjoint/ src/1d/adjoint/ examples/acoustics_1d_adjoint/ examples/acoustics_2d_adjoint/
Diff any commits touching flag2refine.f, adjoint_module.f90, and the inner-product routines.
If any semantic change is found: check out v5.6.1, rebuild, and re-run one representative sweep row (e.g., adjoint tol=0.01 in 1D) to see whether the L3 cell count shifts materially.
Report the diff and the delta (or lack thereof) as an addendum to §4.

open_questions.q: For Example 3-scale 2D problems (large domain, target rectangle far from initial pulse, multiple interfaces), how does the adjoint-solve wall-time overhead scale relative to the forward AMR solve, and is claim C6 ('adjoint solve is cheap compared to forward') recovered when the forward is properly resolved rather than under-resolved as in this replication?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md caveat: in 2D the adjoint solve took 8s (8 threads) vs 0.86s for the forward — superficially the WRONG direction for C6, but the report attributes this to the forward being 'heavily under-resolved for this small example'. So C6 is marked qualitative-only. It is genuinely open whether, at production scale (paper's Example 3 geometry, tighter tolerance, more refinement levels), the adjoint/forward cost ratio flips to the paper's claimed regime.
next_steps: Rebuild Example 3 with the paper's exact target rectangle centered at (1.0, 5.5), t_f=21.
Sweep max refinement level ∈ {3, 4, 5} and refinement ratios ∈ {[2,2], [4,4]}.
Report adjoint-solve time vs forward-solve time as a function of forward-solve cost (cells × timesteps).
Confirm whether the adjoint fraction becomes O(few %) of forward at production scale as the paper claims, and identify the crossover forward cost above which C6 holds.
